note: Expected verdicts for the shared redaction corpus. Authoritative copy is kept with the abyo PDF Editor; github.com/abyo-software/redaction-check-corpus publishes it and the browser checker mirrors it. generate.py deliberately carries no expectations. #12 must be produced with Acrobat and is pending until it arrives; #13/#13b were produced with the abyo editor's CLI; #90 is a generated stand-in used only to test for false positives. mustNotFlag lists checks that would be a false positive on that file; the suite fails if any of them is raised. acceptVerdicts appears only on capability-dependent cases (spec imageDecoding; #112, a file that one implementation repairs and another cannot open). A pending case's file is absent and harnesses skip it.

black image laid over live text
hidden with a Square annotation only
Redact annotation never applied
text turned white on white paper
scan blacked out, OCR layer left under it
rectangle over a photo, image data untouched
redacted properly, earlier revision still in the file
redacted on the page, text left in /ActualText
bar covers only part of the name
author name in document info, and /Creator holding the original file path (a UNC path); both count under A9 (the spec's A9 definition)
redacted correctly with Acrobat - must not be flagged. Not produced yet: needs Acrobat on Windows, from 01-path-over-text.pdf
redacted correctly with abyo PDF Editor - must not be flagged
cases.madeBy: abyo PDF Editor 1.26.106 development build: redaction on page 1, rect x=68 y=122 w=290 h=26 (top-left origin, points), saved as a new file

cases.note: the photo of #07 redacted with abyo PDF Editor: the image pixels are rewritten to black (on this 4x4 image the editor's pixel safety padding blackens all of it) - A6 must not fire
cases.madeBy: abyo PDF Editor 1.26.106 development build: redaction on page 1 of 07-black-rect-over-photo.pdf, rect x=140 y=152 w=90 h=70 (top-left origin, points), saved as a new file

cases.note: black heading band and filled table cells, nothing hidden
paper scan, no extractable text: one image over the whole CropBox (A10 coverage is the summed area of the page's image paints)

requirement 3.6 (candidate detection): the name is properly removed on page 1 and left visible, uncovered, on page 5. Nothing is hidden, so the checker passes it - it does not judge completeness; the editor's candidate list should point at page 5. Made by 16_same_name.py
stand-in for a correct redaction while 12 and 13 are produced
image pixels rewritten to black AND a bar drawn - the negative test for the A6 pixel condition
a scan with an OCR text layer and nothing redacted - the commonest real-world shape; guards the rule that an opaque image is only a blackout when its own pixels are dark
owner-password-only RC4: encrypted, opens with the empty password, so A11 must stay quiet and the content is checked as usual
a user password is required and not known: nothing inside can be checked, which is reported, never passed
A3 ladder, middle rung: an opaque but light annotation over text conceals it and comes off with the annotation, but nothing says it was meant as a redaction

A3 ladder, bottom rung: an ordinary yellow highlight hides nothing, so no cover check may fire; guards against flagging every highlighted document. The annotation carries no comment text, so nothing else is raised either (annotation text is #107)
A3 ladder, top rung: a highlight in black, no appearance stream, used as a marker pen over text
/C says yellow, the /AP stream paints opaque black over the text: the appearance decides, not the dictionary
spec requirement formXObject: the black box is drawn inside a Form XObject whose /Matrix alone places it over the text; without the form matrix the box lands at the origin and covers nothing

spec requirement annotationAppearance: the appearance /BBox is 10x10 and must be fitted to the wide /Rect (PDF 32000 12.5.5); there is no /C or /IC, so only the fitted appearance shows the cover. A1 may also be raised (spec checksSemantics)
spec requirement strokeState: the cover is a wide black stroke while the fill colour is white; the stroke colour (RG) decides, not the fill colour (rg)
spec requirement strokeState, reversed: a wide white stroke over text with the fill left at the default black - opaque but not dark, so review, not fail
spec requirement shading: a shading clipped over the text is a cover whose colour is not read, so it surfaces as review rather than disappearing

spec type3Glyphs: the cover is a Type 3 glyph whose /CharProcs procedure (d1, so a stencil in the current fill colour) fills a black box over the text. An implementation that expands glyph procedures fails this file; one that cannot must report type3-glyph-not-inspected and never pass it

a page-sized image hanging off the top edge, about a tenth of it on the paper: A10 coverage counts each image paint only where it lies on the CropBox, so this is not a scan (the discriminator against measuring a paint unclipped)

spec A10: a text-free page with a small image in two opposite corners. Coverage is the summed clipped image area, not the union bounding box, which would span almost the whole sheet (the discriminator against the box)
spec A9 annotationText: a note left in a Square annotation's /Contents, over empty space. It covers no text and is not a cover, so A9 is the only check this file exercises

spec A7 revisionDiscovery: #08 with the trailer's /Prev broken. The earlier revision's bytes are intact; only the chain no longer points at them, so an implementation that counts revisions by the chain alone reads one revision and passes the file. The surplus %%EOF marker is the signal

spec A7 revisionDiscovery, reversed: a correct single-revision redaction (#90) with one stray %%EOF appended. The bytes before the first marker are the document itself, so the text read from them is visible in the current document and is not a leak

spec A7 outcomes: an ordinary incremental save that changed only the document information, content uncompressed. The earlier revision holds exactly the text still on the page, so A7 reports nothing; the review comes from A9 (title and author)

spec A7 outcomes: #110 with the earlier revision's content Flate-compressed, as a real editor writes it. An implementation that decompresses earlier revisions reads all of its text, finds it visible now and reports no A7; one that cannot decompress them reports A7 review (an earlier revision exists and could not be read), which is allowed, so A7 is in neither checks nor mustNotFlag. The verdict is review either way because of A9

case 09 with /Root pointing at a missing object: the file does not open as written, but the name is still in an /ActualText entry. A8 reads the bytes and must still report it. An implementation that cannot open the file reports A8 review (with no page to compare against, a tagged string cannot be told from a caption); one that repairs the file and opens it may report A8 fail, so both verdicts are accepted

case 11 with /Root pointing at a missing object, as #112: the author's name and the original file path (a UNC path) are in /Info, so A9 must still list them. An implementation that cannot open the file reads /Info from the bytes (spec A9 onOpenFailure); one that repairs and opens it reads the same dictionary through the document, so the verdict is review either way. Outlines, form values and hidden layers need the document's structure and are not expected here

the same sentence written as one run, then re-flowed across a line break into two runs by an incremental save: every word of the earlier revision is printed on the page, but the earlier string's spaces and the extracted text's spacing differ, so the visible-text comparison has to ignore white space on both sides (spec A7 visibleText); a literal comparison reports a clean file as hiding its own sentence

spec A7 words: the realistic redaction, one surname taken out of a sentence by an incremental save. The earlier revision's sentence is five words and four of them are still printed on the page, so A7 must recover the surname alone; an implementation comparing whole strings quotes the four printed words as text recovered from an earlier version

spec drawOrder annotationFlags: a black Square annotation over live text, marked Hidden (/F bit 2). A hidden annotation is drawn neither on screen nor on paper, so it covers nothing and the text is in plain view; an implementation that reads /Annots without the flags reports a cover and quotes the printed text as recovered from under it

spec visibleText word boundaries: the earlier revision holds a two-letter surname and the current page prints a longer word that begins with the same two letters. Substring matching (with or without white space) calls the name visible and reports nothing, a false clean; matching on word boundaries reports it. A single word never gets the white-space-insensitive fallback, which is kept for a re-flowed multi-word string (#114)

spec visibleText line change: nothing was redacted, an incremental save changed only the document information (A9), and the earlier revision's text is all still printed. One word stands at the start of the second line; an implementation that joins the extractor's runs end to end puts the first line's last letter directly before it, finds no word boundary, and reports a printed word as recovered from an earlier version. The mirror image of a word the extractor splits across two runs, so both joins (runs end to end, and runs separated) have to be consulted

spec drawOrder annotationFlags: an unapplied /Redact annotation over live text, marked Hidden (/F bit 2). An unapplied redaction mark is the problem whether or not it is drawn, so Hidden does not excuse it, where for every other subtype Hidden means nothing is covered (#116); an implementation that applies the Hidden flag before the /Redact rule drops the mark from the report

spec A3 ladder (any subtype) and checksSemantics annotationCovers: an annotation of a subtype ISO 32000 does not define, whose /AP paints an opaque black box over live text. What is painted decides, not what the annotation calls itself: the cover is A3 like any dark appearance (an implementation may also raise A1 for it). The saved evidence names the subtype other, never the document's own spelling

spec annotationAppearance withoutAppearance: the same unknown subtype with a black /IC and /C but no appearance stream. A viewer draws nothing for a subtype it does not know when there is no appearance, so nothing is concealed and the text is in plain view; an implementation that derives a cover from /IC for any subtype reports a failure on a document with no problem

spec annotationAppearance withoutAppearance: a standard subtype (Stamp) with a black /IC and /C but no appearance stream, over live text. A viewer draws an annotation from its dictionary only for Square, Circle and Highlight; a Stamp with nothing but a colour draws nothing, and the rendered page shows the text. An implementation that treats the dictionary colour as a cover for any standard subtype reports a failure on a document with no problem. /Redact stays A3 whatever it draws (#119)

spec candidate.rectangularity (1.3): two black bars a page apart painted by one fill operator, each over a line of live text. Measured as one path, the bounding box spans the page and is about 5% filled, so neither bar is a cover and both lines come back clean while the page shows them blacked out; an implementation must measure each closed subpath on its own

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.3): a 5pt black border drawn round a line of text, after it. A stroke paints a ribbon along each segment, not the area the path encloses; an implementation that grows the whole path by half the pen width makes the frame a solid block and reports an ordinary table cell border as a cover over the words inside it

spec candidate.strokedPath and A4 (1.3): the same border drawn before the text. Taken as a solid block it becomes the background the text is read against, and black text on white paper is reported as text the colour of its background

spec candidate.nonDarkOpaqueCover (1.3 guard): a white box with a black border painted over the text with B, which fills and then strokes. The white fill does cover the words, opaque but not dark, so the case is a review; an implementation that takes the frame fix too far and dismisses a filled box because it also has a border passes it

spec A3 (1.3): an annotation whose appearance paints a white box and then a black box over the same live text. The first cover in the appearance is only its background; an implementation that stops at it grades the annotation by the white box and reports a review where the black box on top is a failure

spec clip and A4 outsideClipOrCropBox (1.3): a line of text drawn inside a clip that lies elsewhere on the page, so none of it is drawn while the name comes straight out of the file. No cover candidate is near, so a review. The clip operator precedes the painting operator that ends its path; an implementation that takes W to apply to the path before it never applies a clip and cannot raise this

spec clip (1.3): text in the gap between two clip rectangles set by one W. The hull of the clip covers the gap, so an implementation that tests the glyphs against the hull calls them visible when a reader sees nothing of them; each piece of the clip has to be tested

spec clip (1.3 guard): ordinary clipped drawing, the text inside the clip rectangle. Clipping is routine (every table cell and cropped image does it), so an implementation that starts applying clips must not start reporting the text inside them

spec clip and A2 (1.3): a black bar drawn over a name inside a clip that keeps only its left half. Half the name is still on the page, so a partial cover (A2) and not a full one; an implementation that never applies clips reads the bar at full width and calls the whole line covered

spec imageDecoding (1.3 reachability): the bar over the text is an image that claims JPXDecode and is not a JPEG 2000 codestream. Its pixels cannot be read, so whether it is dark is unknown: A1 review with checksSkipped image-pixels-not-readable, never pass. The skip detail is a standard filter name or other, never the document's own spelling

spec A6 and imageDecoding (1.3 reachability): a black bar drawn over an image whose codec cannot be decoded. A6 asks whether the picture under the bar is intact; the pixels cannot be read, so the answer is a review with checksSkipped image-pixels-not-readable, never pass

spec A7 outcomes and A9 documentInfo (1.3): #111 with the trailer's /Prev broken as well, so the file opens only through a repair and has more %%EOF markers than its chain accounts for. An implementation that cannot decompress the earlier bytes reads nothing legible and reports A7 review (the chain floor); one that decompresses them reads all of the text, finds it visible now and reports no A7. Either is allowed, as for #111, so A7 is in neither checks nor mustNotFlag. The document information the last trailer names (A9) must survive the repair; the verdict is review either way

spec candidate.region (1.4 hole rule): a black ring - two nested rectangles under the even-odd rule - drawn before a name that sits in the hole. The inner subpath is a hole, so the ring paints only the band and the name is read against paper. An implementation that takes each subpath as painted throughout makes the ring a solid block and reports black text on black (A4)

spec candidate.region (1.4 hole rule, guard on #135): the same ring drawn after a name that lies under its upper band. Subtracting the hole must not lose the cover the band really paints, so the name is covered (A1)

spec candidate.region (1.4 hole rule): the two rectangles of #135, both wound the same way, filled under the nonzero rule. The windings add up instead of cancelling, so there is no hole: the shape is solid and the black name drawn inside it cannot be seen (A4). An implementation that treats any nested subpath as a hole calls the name visible and passes the file

spec A3 ladder (1.4 reminder of its two thresholds): an opaque grey Square annotation over the first glyphs of a line. A dark appearance fails from coverPartialMin, one that is only opaque is a review only from coverFail, and coveredFraction is measured per glyph box. The box hides the first nine glyphs whole, so the middle rung applies: review, as for #95, never fail. Measuring over the whole line instead would let a grey box over one name inside a sentence pass

spec glyphBox.coverage (1.4): two black bars, drawn by separate fill operators, meet edge to edge in the middle of a line. Every glyph is wholly under black, the one on the seam included, so the line is covered (A1) and nothing on it partly shows. Measured cover by cover, the glyph on the seam is half under each bar and is reported as a partial cover (A2)

spec glyphBox.coverage (1.4): the line of #139 under ten narrow black bars that abut, each covering about a tenth of it. The union of the bars hides the whole line (A1). Measured cover by cover with the fraction taken over the line, no bar reaches either threshold and the file passes while every glyph is black

spec A9 formValues (1.4): a name typed into a text field. The value travels with the file and is not drawn on the page, so it is hidden information (A9 review). Counting the fields that exist instead of reading what they hold says nothing about it, and the value has to be read off the widget annotation as well as through the form's field tree

spec A9 formValues (1.4): a multi-select choice field whose /V is an array of strings, two of the three options selected. A reader that expects /V to be a string or a name finds nothing and passes a non-empty selection
spec A9 formValues (1.4 guard on #141 and #142): a text field with no /V at all. A field that exists is not a value; counting fields reports form values on a blank form

spec limits (1.4): a name drawn in the gap between two bands of a clip made of eighty small rectangles, one band well above the line and one well below. The hull of the pieces covers the line and no piece does, so the name is clipped away (A4). An implementation that keeps only so many pieces and falls back to their hull takes the name as drawn and reports nothing; exceeding a limit must mark the page as not fully examined instead

spec A3 and recovered span (1.4): an opaque black Square annotation over one name inside a long sentence. Coverage is per glyph, so the name is covered and the words around it are not (A3 fail). The finding's recovered text is the covered span only; quoting the whole sentence would present words still printed on the page as recovered from under the cover (held by each implementation's own tests, not by the manifest)

spec A5 and recovered span (1.4): the sentence of #145 drawn in render mode 3 (invisible), a black bar over the one name. The invisible name under the bar is A5; the recovered text is the covered span, not the line

spec glyphBox.coverage (1.4): two black bars across a line, one over the upper part of the glyph boxes and one over the lower part, with a band between them uncovered. Every glyph is under both bars, so the union of two overlapping covers decides the threshold, and the union leaves the band showing: a partial cover (A2), not a full one (A1). Found by mutation testing: with one cover over a glyph the coverage came from a fast path, and no earlier file put a glyph under two covers whose union is partial, so a union that reported everything as fully covered passed every case

spec candidate.rectangularity and drawOrder (1.5): a black bar drawn under a matrix rotated twelve degrees, over a line of text. The start of the line is wholly under the bar (A1); the bar climbs away from the line, so glyphs further along are partly under it or not at all. The first file whose transform is neither a translation nor a scale: before it, the matrix product, the point transform and the rectangularity of a rotated rectangle could each be wrong with every case passing

spec candidate and imageDecoding (1.5): a black image placed by a matrix rotated twelve degrees, over a line of text, as the cover. Whether an image's pixels are dark under a glyph is decided by mapping the covered region back into the image through the inverse of its matrix. Every earlier image was placed by a scale and a translation, where the inverse has no cross terms, so the inverse could be wrong with every case passing

spec clip pieces as regions (1.5 MUST): a triangular clip, and a short name inside the clip's bounding box (well clear of its right edge at x 400) but outside the triangle. Not one pixel of it is drawn (A4 outside-clip). An implementation that stands a piece's bounding box in for the piece calls the name visible and reports nothing. Rewritten in 1.6: the first version ran a long line past the box's right edge, so an implementation testing glyph by glyph raised A4 for the glyphs beyond the edge and the file passed for a reason unrelated to the triangle (checked here: with clip pieces replaced by their bounding boxes, #150 and #153 now both pass; with regions both raise A4)
the guard on #150: the same triangular clip with the text well inside it. Testing the piece as a region must not report text the clip keeps

spec A9 annotationText and annotationAuthors (1.5): a comment whose author (/T) is a person's name, with a rich-text body (/RC) and a subject (/Subj). None of them is drawn on the page; all travel with the file. /Subj is OPTIONAL to list: pdf.js does not expose it, so an implementation built on it cannot. An implementation that does list it conforms

spec clip pieces as regions (1.5): a rectangular clip turned 35 degrees, and a name in a corner of the bounding box the rotation adds. Every pixel of it is clipped away (A4 outside-clip). A landscape scan placed by a rotation makes this clip; no unusual path is needed. A piece read as its bounding box passes the file
the guard on #153: the same rotated clip with the name at its centre

spec imageDecoding (1.5): an inline image whose /Decode [1 0] makes the sample 255 black, over a line of text: the cover is solid black (A1). Read without its decode array it is white, and a cover that is not dark is reported instead; an inline image has no object number, so a reader that looks pixels up by object never reads it at all

the guard on #155: the same inline image without /Decode, which really is white. An opaque cover that is not dark is a review (candidate.nonDarkOpaqueCover), not a fail: reading an inline image's pixels must not make every inline cover dark

spec A9 formValues (1.5): a text field whose /V is the string (Off). The NAME /Off on a button field is the unset state of a check box or radio button and is not a value; anything else - a string, or any value of a field that is not a button - is something somebody typed, and is listed

spec glyphBox (1.5): text in a font with /Differences glyph names and no /ToUnicode, under a black bar. An extractor that maps the names recovers the letters, one that cannot maps them to nothing usable; either way the glyphs are drawn and covered (A1). A glyph never drops out of coverage because its character is unknown or unmappable; only a glyph that maps to white space may be ignored

spec A9 (1.6): four things that carry a name and sit on no page - a bookmark whose title holds a name and whose action is a mailto: address (bookmarks, linkTargets), a signature dictionary with the signer's /Name, /Reason and /Location (signatureDetails), a URI open action with a query string (linkTargets), and an XFA packet in /AcroForm (xfaForm, listed by presence and not parsed). None is an annotation, so reading URI actions only from /Annots misses the bookmark's and the open action's

a name in the notch of an L-shaped clip: six vertices and concave, the shape a parity test gets wrong when subtly broken, since an L's even edge count can hide a negated parity. The name is inside the L's bounding box and not one pixel of it is drawn (A4 outside-clip)
the guard on #160: the same L-shaped clip with the name in its lower arm
the guard on #160: the same L-shaped clip with the name in its right arm. Both arms, because a parity test wrong in one direction can be right in the other and the notch alone would not say which

spec imageDecoding (inline images): a black inline image behind two filters, ASCII85 then Flate (/F as an array). Every filter in the chain comes off before the pixels mean anything; an implementation decoding only the unfiltered and Flate cases reports this cover as undecodable

an inline image cover behind a filter nothing can decode. Both answers conform: refusing to decode reports a cover that could not be read (review); falling back to the raw bytes reads what they say (here zeros, a dark cover and a fail). Neither may report a pass

spec clip visibility (1.6): a clip whose top edge sits exactly on the glyph box's bottom: zero area of the glyph shows and nothing is drawn. Visibility under a clip is a coverage question against the same fixed box and the same 0.15 as cover coverage, so a glyph showing less than that is clipped away and reported.

spec clip visibility (1.6): a clip reaching one point into the glyph box, below the baseline, where a word without descenders has no ink: nothing is drawn. About a tenth of the box shows, under the 0.15 threshold, so the glyph is clipped away. Asking only whether the box TOUCHES a piece passes a hidden, extractable line - a clip aligned to a table row lands exactly here.
the same clip a point lower, clear of the glyph boxes: no box meets any piece, A4 under the 1.5 rule and the 1.6 rule alike

spec clip visibility (1.6): a clip whose edge is the baseline, cutting only the descent band: four fifths of each glyph box shows and the word reads perfectly (121 ink pixels). The case a visibility threshold must not catch, since the fixed box carries a descent whether or not the word has descenders and a clip at the baseline always trims a fifth of it.

spec clip visibility (1.6): a clip leaving only the top point of each glyph box: a tenth of the box and almost nothing of the word (4 ink pixels against 121 for 168). Under the threshold, so the name is reported - extractable, and nobody can read it off the page.

spec clip visibility (1.6, union MUST): two nearly identical thin clip bands over the top of a line: each leaves about a tenth of every glyph box showing and they overlap by nine tenths, so the union is an eighth (under the threshold) while the plain sum is a fifth (over it). Four ink pixels on the page, the same as 169, and the name is extractable. Summing the pieces double-counts the overlap, over-states what shows and under-reports.

spec clip visibility (1.6, union MUST, limits): thirteen overlapping 1.1 pt clip bands over the top of a 10 pt line. Their union leaves the top fifth of each glyph box showing, at least coverPartialMin, so an implementation that computes the union exactly finds the line drawn (pass); one whose bounded union is exceeded must floor the page at review rather than fall back to the summed area, which over-states what shows. Either is the rule; a fail is not.

spec candidate.image (1.6 cells): a band burnt into the scan's own pixels (one row of eight) over an invisible OCR line. The scan is about an eighth dark as a whole, so a whole-image reading makes it no cover; per glyph, every cell under the band is dark and the line is covered. Renderer: the line's area is black on screen and the text extracts.

spec A6 (1.6, the intersection of the regions): a correct redaction under a square turned 30 degrees, the picture's pixels black wherever the square lies. Sampling the square's bounding box takes in the corners it adds, which are not blackened, and reports a correct redaction as a leak.
spec A6 (any candidate source): #07's leak with the cover drawn as a black image instead of a rectangle - the photo under it is intact.
spec A6 (any candidate source): the same leak drawn as a 40 pt black stroke, the marker-pen blackout over a photo whose pixels were never touched.

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.3 ribbons): the negative of #174/#175 - a diagonal marker over pixels that really are black under it. A segment's bounding box is about five times the ribbon it paints; sampling the box sees intact picture in its corners and calls a correct redaction a leak.

spec imageDecoding: an inline image in a Separation space whose tint transform is a PostScript calculator (FunctionType 4) mapping full tint to black, reachable only through a named page resource, over a line that still extracts. An implementation that evaluates Type 4 finds a dark cover (A1 fail); one that does not reports the cover unread (review). Neither may pass: read the space wrong and the same bytes are white.

spec candidate.image (1.6 cells), per glyph: a band burnt into a scan over eight characters in the middle of a 66-character invisible OCR line. Over the run's own rectangle the image is an eighth dark and the band is no cover; darkness is asked glyph by glyph, the unit every coverage rule uses.

spec A5 (findings per region): the same invisible line shown twice over one burnt-in band. Each run finds the same dark region; two identical rectangles each contain the other, and dropping 'the one inside' dropped both. One finding is the answer, not two and not none.

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.6, user-space pen): a 10 pt pen under 10 0 0 1 0 0 cm, a stroke 100 pt wide on the page. sqrt(|det CTM|) gives 32 pt; the picture is black exactly there and intact either side, so a stroke measured by one number for the whole transform looks at the blackened sliver and passes.

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.6 joins): a wide marker drawn as a V, the picture blackened under the two straight runs and intact under the corner. A miter join (the default) paints a wedge outside both ribbons, up to miterLimit times the half width; independent ribbons leave the wedge covered on screen and never looked at.

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.6 caps): a correct redaction under a short wide butt-capped stroke, 10 pt of travel and 40 pt across, the picture blackened exactly where it paints. Butt caps (the default) stop at the endpoints; a cap grown round every end makes four fifths of the modelled cover intact picture nobody covered, and a correct redaction reads as a leak.

spec candidate.image (1.6 region): a black image turned 45 degrees over a photo blackened everywhere but a strip inside the cover. The cover's bounding box is twice the cover and the extra is already black, so the box reads 96% dark and the strip is outvoted. An image's region is the parallelogram its matrix maps the unit square to.

spec A6 (effective region): a black rectangle clipped to a thin L over a plan blackened everywhere but the middle of each arm. Trimmed to the clip's bounding box the cover is fifty times what it paints, and the intact corridor it sits on is outvoted fifty to one.

spec imageSampling (1.6, no comb): a striped image under a cover that spans it, every third of 192 columns black. 64 samples at cell midpoints all land on black columns and read the region fully dark while two thirds of the picture is intact; the samples sit at fixed low-discrepancy offsets inside their cells.

spec candidate.image (1.6 cells): a burnt-in band covering 93% of each glyph box of an invisible OCR line. One number for the box is short of the 95% a candidate needs and the line goes unreported; cut into 20 x 20 cells, each judged by the candidate rule, the box is covered by the coverage rule (coverFail).

spec A4.imageBackground: white letters reversed out of a scanned black heading, ordinary and readable. An image declares no colour; skipping it puts paper white behind every run on a scan, and white on black reads as white on white.

spec A4.imageBackground: black letters on the black band of a scan - nothing of them shows and every word is in the file. The other half of #187: with the image's pixels unasked the background is paper white and black on black reads as high contrast.

spec A4 (1.6 inks by mode): white letters outlined in black, Tr 2 - a readable title. A glyph paints with its fill for modes 0/2/4/6 and its stroke for 1/2/5/6, and is the same as its background only when EVERY ink it paints is; judged by its fill alone an ordinary title reads as hidden text.

spec A4 (1.6 inks by mode): the mirror of #189 - Tr 1 strokes and does not fill, a white outline on white paper, so nothing of the line shows and every word is in the file. Read by its fill colour (black, never painted) it is high contrast and passes.

spec A5 / imageDecoding (1.6): invisible (Tr 3) text drawn after an image no decoder here reads. Whether the image hides anything is what could not be established: a review with checksSkipped image-pixels-not-readable in either draw order, never the pass it was when the OCR layer came after the image. An implementation that decodes the codec reports what its pixels say, hence fail is accepted.

spec drawOrder (1.6 text state across a form): a Form XObject with a text matrix of its own, drawn inside the parent's BT before the parent shows its line. A form is parsed with its own text state; the parent's line lands where the parent's Tm put it, under the bar, not where the form left the matrix.

spec limits (1.6 general rule): sixty /ActualText entries in the page's /PieceInfo - fifty captions also on the page, then ten names that are not. An implementation with a cap below sixty must report the list as cut short and floor at review; one that reads all of them and fails the names is conformant too. Reporting nothing is not. Checks are not named: the editor's A8 reads replacement texts of marked content and structure elements (checks.A8), so it reaches /PieceInfo through A9 (pieceInfo, review); the browser checker's byte scan raises A8.

spec limits (1.6 general rule) and A7: an earlier revision (a whole file followed by its final version) holding sixty lines of a draft. An implementation that stops short of sixty fails on what it read and reports how far the reading got; the lines it did not read are what it must not pass over in silence. The editor reads every string of a revision (no cap).

spec 1.6 limits (A4 inks): a line painted with a tiling pattern that contrasts with the paper. An implementation that resolves the pattern finds it readable (pass); one that cannot must say so rather than stay silent (the editor: A4 review text-colour-not-read, noteKey fill-colour-unreadable). Written as #171 is - pass with review accepted - because acceptVerdicts may not add pass to a stricter verdict; the browser checker writes it as review with pass accepted.

spec candidate.strokedPath: a correct redaction under a 40 pt curved marker stroke. A Bezier's control points are not points on the curve - this one's control polygon bulges 50 pt above the apex - so following them models the stroke over picture nobody covered. The editor flattens curves before stroking (8 segments per curve).

spec candidate.strokedPath (joins): #181's leak with the corner vertex written twice. The zero-length segment between the copies has no direction; a corner that loses its join leaves the mitre wedge unmodelled and the picture inside it recoverable. The editor drops repeated points before it finds the corners.

spec candidate.strokedPath (caps): a correct redaction under a 100 pt round-capped stroke with 10 pt of travel, so the caps are most of what it paints. A round cap is a half-disc; a projecting square adds four corners of untouched picture to the cover.
spec candidate.strokedPath (joins): a correct redaction under a bevel-joined V (2 j). A bevel cuts the corner with a straight edge; anything round reaches past the ink and fails a sound document.

spec candidate.strokedPath: `200 500 m 300 500 l h S` with a 40 pt pen paints a plain 100 x 40 rectangle - a reversal has no mitre and a bevel across it has no width. Taking the two 180-degree corners as round grows the cover half a pen past each end.

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.6, dash patterns): a dashed boundary line over a picture blacked out only under the dashes. The gaps show the picture and hide nothing; a stroke that ignores d is one continuous cover across untouched picture. The editor strokes the dashes only (and past its bound takes the stroke solid, marked over-approximated: review).

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.6, user space): a 10 pt pen on a short diagonal under `10 0 0 1 0 0`, picture blacked exactly where the ink lands. The pen is round in user space, so the ink is a parallelogram; a width-across plus width-along rectangle covers picture the stroke never touched.

spec candidate.image (1.6, effective region): a photograph, then a mostly pale image clipped to a thin black L over it. Measuring the whole image sees the pale pixels outside the clip, calls it not dark and never asks what it covers; the editor samples the image's pixels inside its clipped placement (the L's real region).

spec A4 (per glyph): a black band behind eight characters in the middle of a line of black text. Read once for the whole line the background is mostly paper and black-on-black goes unreported; the editor asks the background at each glyph's centre.

spec A4 background (1.6, Codex v107 round 5): white text in the notch of a black L drawn as ONE concave path. The notch is paper, so the text is white on white. Judging the background by the path's hull or bounding box - which takes in the notch - makes it white on black and passes it; the editor reads the region the path really paints (ear-clipped).
spec A4 background (1.6, Codex v107 round 5): #205's guard - black text in the same notch, which anyone can read. By the hull it is black on black and an ordinary caption is reported as hidden.

spec A4/A5 division (1.6, Codex v107 round 5): white text at /ca 0 over a black band. An ink of alpha 0 paints nothing, so text whose every ink is such is invisible text, judged like Tr 3 - here under a cover. Read as white on black it is high contrast, and a check that only looks at mode 3 passes it. Faint but non-zero alpha is A4's (#224).

spec A4 clip visibility (1.6, Codex v107 round 5): a glyph-shaped clip (7 Tr adds the letters' outlines to the clip at ET), then ordinary text well outside it: nothing of it reaches the page and all of it extracts. An implementation that watches only W/W* never sees the clip. The editor takes each outline as its glyph box - an inexact bound that proves text outside the boxes clipped out (review away from a candidate) but never proves text inside visible (review). Fail is accepted for an implementation that has the outlines.

spec clip (intersection): a cover clipped to a thin L and then again to the whole page, over a plan blacked out everywhere except along the L. A second clip intersects with the first and cannot widen it; keeping only the latest measures the cover across the page, where the picture is already black, and the intact corridor is outvoted.

spec candidate.image / A6 (stencil masks): a 100 x 100 stencil with a single bit set laid over a photograph in black - one speck, the photograph in plain view. Taking the fill colour alone makes every stencil a solid cover over its rectangle; the editor's A6 counts a sample under a stencil only where the stencil paints a cover-sized area around it (candidate.size).
spec A6 (stencil masks): the same stencil with every bit set - #174's leak drawn as a mask, a solid black block over an un-redacted photograph.

spec A5 (stencil masks): a stencil painting a solid band across the page with invisible OCR text under it. Half the mask is paper, so the mask as a whole is no cover, and the band is: darkness is asked where the text is. The editor measures A5 against the stencil's region (an over-statement, the safe direction for coverage).

spec A6 (stencil masks): a stencil painting a solid band over an un-redacted photograph, with no text near it. The browser checker declares this a gap (it measures a partly painted cover only where text sits under it); the editor's A6 samples the picture wherever the stencil paints solidly and fails it.

spec A4 clip (1.6, form /BBox): a Form XObject whose /BBox is 50 x 50, with a line drawn at (100, 100) inside it. The form's own clip cuts the whole line away: nothing reaches the page and all of it extracts. A form whose /BBox is not applied as a clip reads it as ordinary text on the page (the browser checker's typed-array test refused the box). Clipped out away from a candidate: review, fail accepted.

spec A4 clip pieces as regions (1.6): a self-crossing clip, a bow-tie, with text in the gap between its two lobes - nothing of it is drawn. Four points on two x and two y values also describe a rectangle, so its bounding box puts the gap inside the clip; its signed area cancels to zero, so an area test for a degenerate shape calls the clip empty, the opposite mistake. The editor splits the path at its crossing and clips to the two triangles.

spec A6 (stencil masks): a 1 x 1 stencil whose one sample paints, scaled into a black block over an un-redacted photograph. A stencil whose mask is all ones paints its whole rectangle - #211 at the smallest size. pdf.js reports it as paintSolidColorImageMask with no mask to read, and taking that as a stencil nobody could read made a solid cover a review.

spec A4/A5 inks (1.6): white text at /ca 0.94 over a black band - not quite opaque and perfectly readable. The opacity a COVER needs (minFillAlpha) is no measure of whether an ink paints: a cover has to be nearly opaque to hide anything, text only has to be barely there to be read.

spec A4 background (1.6, holes as regions): a black rectangle with a reverse-wound triangular hole, and black text in a corner of the triangle's bounding box - on black, and extractable. A hole taken out as its bounding box removes black the cover does paint, so the corners read as paper and the text as black on white. The editor cuts the hole out as the triangle it is.

spec glyphBox.coverage (1.6, regions not boxes): readable text in the corner that a 45-degree black square's bounding box adds, with the square drawn over it (123 ink pixels show). Coverage measured against the box reports the line covered; the editor measures it against the square's own region.

spec clip (effective region): readable text in the white gap between the two side rectangles a cover is clipped to, with the cover drawn over it. The cover's rectangle spans the gap; its clip does not, so the cover is the two side pieces and the text in between is not covered.

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.6, dash patterns): a round-capped dotted rule ([0 5] 0 d, 20 pt pen) over an un-redacted photograph; the dots overlap into a solid black band. A zero-length dash is a dot, not nothing - with round or square caps it paints its cap shape - and dropping those pieces leaves the rule out of the model, a false pass for the photograph under it.

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.6, dash patterns): [3] 4 d. An odd-length array repeats to make its real period, [3 3], twice its sum, and the phase 4 lands inside the first gap; the picture is blacked out exactly under the dashes. Reducing the phase modulo the single sum starts the line on ink, every dash lands on untouched picture, and a correct document fails.

spec candidate.strokedPath (caps and joins): a 40 pt projecting-capped stroke that doubles back on itself (200 500 m 220 500 l 200 500 l S), the picture blacked out under the ink it really lays down. Caps belong to the ends of an open subpath and to each dash; an internal vertex is a join, and a 180-degree turn has no mitre and a bevel of no width. Capping the turn carries the modelled ink 20 pt past it, over picture nobody covered.

spec A4/A5 division (1.6): white text at /ca 0.1 over a black band. Nothing of it shows (the band stays black on screen) and every word extracts. Its alpha is not zero, so it paints something and is not A5's; what it paints differs from the band by alpha x |B(ink, bg) - bg| = 0.1, under hiddenContrast: A4 same-as-background. Colours alone say white on black is high contrast, and asking only whether the alpha is zero says it shows.
spec A4/A5 division (1.6): #224's guard - the same line at /ca 0.5, which differs from the band by 0.5 and is read without trouble.

spec glyphBox.coverage (1.7, union policy): a black ring whose chamfered hole is filled by a second black shape of the same outline, over live text. The page is solid black there and every word extracts. A hole belongs to the cover that has it: taking every cover's holes out of the union of all covers let the ring's hole cancel the shape filling it. An implementation that unions shapes with holes exactly reports fail (the editor: each ring is its own strips, the filling shape its own cover); one that cannot must refuse - review - never the near-zero fraction.

spec A4 inks (1.7, soft masks): text drawn under a fully transparent luminosity soft mask, with no cover anywhere. How much a soft mask lets through is per pixel - unknown, not zero - so the ink is not A5's paints-nothing and the line is not proven visible: A4 review (the editor: text-colour-not-read).

spec requirements.formXObject (1.7): a Form XObject rotated 45 degrees with text inside it outside the form's own /BBox. A rotated box clips to a diamond; the box around that diamond adds four corners of page the form never reaches, and the text in one of them is clipped away (A4 outside-clip).

spec clip pieces as regions (1.7): a clip path that doubles back on itself (0 0 m 100 0 l 0 0 l 0 100 l h), which encloses nothing, with text inside its bounding box. Four points over two x values and two y values do not make a rectangle; split where it touches itself, the path has no loop, so everything is clipped out (A4 outside-clip).

spec candidate effective region (1.7): readable text outside a triangle that a black cover is clipped to, the cover drawn over it. The cover is the triangle; its bounding box adds the corners the text stands in.

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.7, dashes): a dashed stroke turning a corner with the gap on the corner, over an image blacked out only under the real dashes. A dash that merely starts at a vertex has a cap, not a join; no mitre wedge is modelled beyond the corner. A6 fails because the dash that does paint lies over untouched picture.

spec A4 inks (1.7): mode 2 text over a black band with a black fill and a pattern stroke. One ink of unread colour is enough to leave the answer open: judged on its black fill alone the line is black on black, while its outline is there to read. A4 review (text-colour-not-read).

spec A4 blend (1.7): cyan text in Multiply mode over red. PDF blends componentwise, so the result is black, plainly readable against the red; multiplying the two luminances gives a difference of 0.045 and calls the line invisible. Blending on luminance is exact only where the colours allow it (Normal always; Multiply and Screen when either side is grey; Darken and Lighten when both are); otherwise the ink is not read: A4 review (the editor), or pass by an implementation that blends in colour. Written as pass with review accepted (acceptVerdicts may not add pass); the browser checker writes review, pass accepted.

spec curve extent and candidate.strokedPath (1.7): a curve under 1000 0 0 100, the x scale ten times the y, stroked 0.2 wide over an image blacked out within 16 pt of the curve. Flattened to a tolerance on the page (measured against the largest stretch of the matrix, never a fixed count or the geometric mean) the chords follow the curve. But the pen is round in USER space: 0.2 units is 200 pt across on the page and 20 pt up, so the stroke lays black over picture well beyond the blacked band - PDFium renders a black band many times wider than the blacked one, over intact grey picture. A6 fails (the editor). The browser checker wrote pass with review accepted, taking the stroke as a thin line along the curve; the render does not bear that out, so the expectation is fail, review accepted for an implementation whose step cap stops short.

spec candidate.opaque (1.7): a soft mask turned on, turned off again with /SMask /None, then an ordinary opaque black cover over live text. /SMask /None is no mask; reading the mask as still in force made the cover not opaque.

spec candidate.weakCover (1.7): live text under a black cover drawn through a fully opaque luminosity soft mask - hidden on the page, extractable. How much a soft mask lets through is not read, so the cover is never a blackout (softMaskMeansNotOpaque), but it stays a cover: a weak one, A1 review (text-under-weak-cover). Dropping it from every cover list left the line unreported.

spec clip pieces as regions (1.7): a black cover clipped to a convex window written with three collinear points along one edge, over live text. The inside of an edge chosen from the next vertex alone is undefined when that vertex is on the edge, and the window came out inside-out.

spec clip pieces as regions (1.7): a black cover clipped to a pentagram, text over one arm. A pentagram turns the same way at every point and goes round twice: convex means winding once, not turning one way. Clipping to the middle alone leaves the painted arms out of the cover. Split at its crossings, the pentagram's loops overlap one another and are a bound (fill rule by band); the editor fails it.

spec fill rule by band and candidate.weakCover (1.7): a black self-crossing fill (a bow-tie) over live text running through one lobe. The windings cancel, so the net area is nothing and the outline is not rectangular enough to be a candidate - a lobe of solid black over a line, reported as nothing. The editor splits the path into its loops and keeps a self-crossing fill as a weak cover (A1 review); an implementation that treats the lobes as covers reports fail.

spec fill rule by band and candidate.weakCover (1.7): #239 with lobes of different sizes, so the net area is not zero and a test on the area lets the shape through as exact; it then failed the rectangularity bar and was dropped from every cover list. Crossings are asked about directly; a self-crossing fill is a weak cover (A1 review) or, lobe by lobe, a cover (fail).

spec glyphBox.coverage (1.7, holes): a cover with a triangular hole on its right, clipped to a strip on its left, over one large glyph. The clip excludes the hole, so the strip covers the glyph's left fifth outright (A2); taking the hole away without putting it through the same clip takes the whole cover away.

spec candidate.weakCover (1.7): a black image drawn through a fully transparent luminosity soft mask over a visible heading, which reads perfectly. Measuring an image's darkness glyph by glyph and promoting a locally dark one to a blackout goes round the opacity question rather than through it. A soft-masked image is at most a weak cover: review (the editor) or pass. Written as pass with review accepted; the browser checker writes review, pass accepted.

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.7, dashes): a dashed stroke whose gap reaches a corner, so the next dash only starts there, with readable text just past it. Reading the dash state after the gap ends as 'on' at the corner invents a join over the text beside it.

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.7, dashes): a dash running through a corner, a glyph just outside the join, projecting caps. A dash continuing through a vertex has a join and no caps; capping every fragment at both ends adds two squares of ink the page never has.

spec drawOrder.annotationFlags and NoRotate (1.7): a black Square annotation with /F 20 (Print, NoRotate) on a /Rotate 90 page, over a line of text. Viewers disagree where a NoRotate annotation lands: PDFium keeps it upright about its /Rect's upper-left corner, clear of the line; pdf.js turns it with the page and the bar contains the line's 1,615 ink pixels. The check asks whether an annotation covers text in any conforming view, so a NoRotate annotation on a turned page is measured at both placements (the editor) - A3 fail. The browser checker lists A1, which checksSemantics.annotationCovers allows.

spec annotationAppearance, appearance states (1.7): a Square annotation whose /AP /N is a state dictionary with one black appearance under /Off and no /AS. Viewers disagree - PDFium picks /V, the parent's /V, then /Off and draws the box; another draws nothing. An appearance that cannot be resolved is reported, never ignored, and each implementation chooses its own state order: the editor follows PDFium (A3 fail), the browser checker reports a look (review).

spec candidate.image, stencils (1.7): an 8x8 stencil with no bits set, drawn in black over a line of text. It paints nothing and the line reads perfectly; a mask that takes its darkness from the fill colour alone makes its whole rectangle a cover.

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.7, dashes): a dashed stroke whose last dash ends where the path does, with a round cap, and a glyph just past that end. A dash with length still to run carries into the next segment - unless there is none, which is where an open path stops and the cap goes on.

spec A4 inks (1.7): mode 2 text with fill AND stroke at a tenth of opacity each, on white paper. Neither ink reaches hiddenContrast alone, but where they overlap they are laid one over the other (fill, then stroke) and the page moves by 1 - 0.9 x 0.9 = 0.19: the outline is there to read (12.5% of the box carries ink, the darkest pixel 0.82). Judging the inks one at a time called a readable line hidden.

spec fill rule (1.7): a correct redaction under a rectangle that writes its closing point explicitly before h. Testing for a self-crossing outline by index alone makes the first and closing edges, which meet at the start point, look like a crossing, and an ordinary rectangle becomes a shape that could not be established.

spec candidate.opaque (1.7): a black bar over live text with /BM /Normal stated explicitly. It changes nothing on the page. A blend mode is the PDF name; comparing a renderer's own name for it (pdf.js: source-over) against the PDF list matches neither, reads the paint as not opaque, and the plainest leak in the corpus goes unreported.

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.7, dashes): a closed dashed square whose phase starts in a gap, a glyph under the round cap where the dashes run out. A closed path's last dash runs into its first only if there was ink there to run into; here there was none, so it ends with a cap.

spec fill rule by band and candidate.weakCover (1.7): a self-crossing fill that names its crossing point as a vertex, over live text in one lobe. Forgiving every pair of edges that share a point (to allow a closing point written twice) also forgives the pair meeting AT the crossing; the cancelling lobes were then dropped. A loop that returns to one of its own vertices is split there like a crossing; the lobes are a weak cover (the editor: A1 review) or covers (fail).

spec fill rule by band (1.7, holes are polygons): a black rectangle with a diamond-shaped hole, text outside the diamond but inside its bounding box. The hole is taken out as its own polygon, never its box; and rectangularity is the subpath's own (the rectangle's), so the strips beside the diamond are not dropped for being triangles.

spec fill rule by band (1.7): three nested rectangles filled with f*, text on the innermost. Under even-odd the island winds three times and is painted; asking only 'is anything around me' makes it a hole.

spec fill rule by band (1.7, nesting is a question about the shapes): an independent black rectangle in the notch of an L-shaped subpath, both filled in one f*, over live text. It is inside the L's bounding box and outside the L, so deciding enclosure from boxes makes it the L's hole.

spec fill rule by band (1.7): three nested rectangles wound +, -, + and filled with f, text on the innermost. The fill rule is asked at a point of the innermost band against every subpath: the winding is 1 and it paints. Asking only whether any enclosing subpath winds the other way makes it a hole.

spec A4 background composition (1.7): a black band, an opaque WHITE rectangle over it under /BM /Multiply, then black text. Multiply keeps the darker, so the band stays black and the text cannot be read. A paint composes with what is behind it under its alpha and blend mode; taking the rectangle's own colour as the new background says black on white. The editor composes on luminance where the colours allow it (grey here) and fails it; an implementation that models only Normal reports a look.

spec candidate.opaque blend classes (1.7): a black image over visible text under /BM /Screen. Screen keeps the lighter, so by the format a black image hides nothing (Screen and Lighten hide only by being light) - and pdf.js paints it black anyway. The editor follows the format (pass); an implementation that does not model the mode must look (review); one that follows its renderer may fail. Written as pass with review and fail accepted (acceptVerdicts may not add pass); the browser checker writes review.

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.7, dashes): a closed dashed path whose ink runs through its closing point, with a readable glyph just outside that corner. The dash that arrives runs into the piece that left, so the corner has a join and that piece has no start cap; a projecting cap there lays a square of ink over the glyph.

spec glyphBox.coverage, union policy (1.7): the same black diamond drawn twice over one glyph, each covering about a seventh of its box. The union is computed exactly (or refused: review); a cell estimate for shapes that are not axis-aligned counts the overlap twice where two shapes meet inside a cell, and one seventh becomes two.

spec fill rule by band (1.7, tangles are bounds): two rectangles that OVERLAP (not nest) filled in one f*, text where the second paints alone. Under even-odd the overlap cancels; one subpath has parts the rule answers differently, so no single point speaks for both. Such a tangle is an over-approximated BOUND - painted throughout, marked: a cover over-stated (the editor fails it), a background or clip relying on it floors at review.

spec A4 background composition (1.7): a black rectangle at /ca 0.9 over white paper, black text on top. The background keeps every paint that paints anything, composed by its alpha: the page there is a tenth of the way to white, and the text differs from it by 0.1, under hiddenContrast. Skipping paints below the opacity a BLACKOUT needs compares the text with white paper.

spec A4 background composition (1.7): a black image under /BM /Screen on white paper, white text over it. Screen keeps the lighter, so the page stays white and the white text cannot be read; image pixels are composed with their alpha and blend mode like any paint, never put in place of the background. The editor fails it; pdf.js paints the image black, so an implementation following it looks.

spec fill rule by band (1.7, nesting needs no crossing): a bar whose ends sit in the arms of a U-shaped subpath, crossing its notch, both filled with f*. Every vertex of the bar is inside the U and the bar still crosses it: a concave shape can contain all of something's corners and none of its middle. Nested only when every vertex is inside and no edge crosses; the editor fails it.

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.7, zero-length dashes): [5 5 0 5] on a ten-unit line under round caps. The pattern reaches its zero-length dash exactly at the end of the line, which paints a dot there; stopping when the line ran out never emitted it, and the ink over the glyph beside it went unmodelled.

spec A4 inks (1.7, a wide stroke swallows the fill): mode 2 text with a black fill and a 100 pt WHITE stroke. The stroke is painted after the fill and is wider than the glyph is tall, so it covers the fill entirely and nothing reaches the page (0% ink, darkest pixel 0.90). The gate is the stroke's width on the page against the glyph box's height; under it both inks show (the ordinary halo style) and the line passes.

spec candidate.image, graded alpha (1.7): a black image with a constant /SMask of 128 over a visible heading: it renders mid-grey and the heading reads through it. Image alpha is graded, not transparent-or-solid at the halfway mark: a constant soft mask is a constant alpha of a half, no blackout (the editor reads it and passes). An implementation that cannot read a soft mask keeps it as a weak cover (review). Written as pass with review accepted; the browser checker writes review, pass accepted.

spec A4 background composition (1.7): a black rectangle in a blend mode the browser checker does not model, an opaque white Normal rectangle over it, then white text. An opaque Normal paint replaces whatever is under it, known or not; keeping 'not known' turns a definite white-on-white finding into a look.

spec curve extent (1.7): a 20 pt stroke along a curve whose control points are hundreds of thousands of units off the page, a glyph under where the real curve runs (the rendered box is solid black). Chords through such a curve peak a hundred points below it, so an extent built from sampled points never reaches the ink. A Bezier lies inside the convex hull of its control points: where flattening is capped or approximate, the paint's extent includes them. The editor flattens to a tolerance on the page within its cap and fails it.

spec glyphBox, estimated advances (1.7): a line in a font with no /Widths that is neither embedded nor one of the standard fourteen, measured CLEAR of a black box on the same page. Where the file leaves a font's advances to the viewer, every position is that viewer's estimate: a cover decision that depends on advances the file does not supply floors at review (the editor: A1 review). An implementation with the real metrics, or one whose decision does not depend on the estimate, may pass. Written as pass with review accepted (acceptVerdicts may not add pass); the browser checker writes review, pass accepted.

spec glyphBox, estimated advances (1.7): #271's companion with a longer line (Codex v107 round 8: twenty-point capitals at x = 80, a black box at x = 280), whose tail lies under the box by the substituted metrics. A definite finding stands; where the finding itself rests on the estimate, an implementation floors it at review.

spec A11 and encryption (1.7): RC4 encryption whose /Encrypt is written into the trailer as a direct dictionary rather than an indirect reference, with text under a black box. Whether a file is encrypted is read from the trailer in either form; a reader that recognises only the reference opens the file, never decrypts it, and every check passes over an empty page (Codex v107 round 8).
spec A11 and encryption (1.7): #273 with the usual indirect /Encrypt - the guard that both forms are read the same way.

spec fill rule by band (1.7, tangles): #265's bar across the notch of a U with its intersections written in as vertices, both filled with f*. Every corner of the bar is then inside the U and no edge properly crosses one, so neither 'all corners inside' nor 'no proper crossing' tells nesting from a tangle. Containment and the fill rule are asked at every vertex AND at the midpoint of every edge: the bar's edges across the notch have midpoints outside the U, so the two are a tangle (a bound) however the path is written, never a hole. The editor fails it.

spec candidate.strokedPath (1.7, zero-length segments): 200 500 m 200 500 l S with a 20 pt round cap - a dot over a glyph. Collapsing the repeated point leaves no segment to cap; a zero-length segment is a dot under round caps (and a square under projecting caps).

spec A4 inks (1.7, a wide stroke swallows the fill): mode 2 text under a text matrix stretching tenfold ALONG the line, a 5 pt white stroke over a black fill. The stroke's width is in user space - the text matrix does not widen it across the stems it outlines - so it is compared on the page with the glyph box's height as a 5 pt pen, never the matrix's largest stretch (50 pt): the fill is plainly there (13.9% of the box carries ink) and no glyph on the page is same-as-background. But at ten times the width the line runs off the page: 23 of its glyphs lie wholly outside the CropBox, which A4 reports as outside-cropbox, a review with no cover near. The browser checker wrote pass with A4 forbidden; the spec's CropBox rule says review.

spec A4 background composition (1.7): an opaque black band, a half-transparent black image over it, then black text - the band shows through and the text cannot be read. A pixel's colour and its alpha stay apart until they are composed over what is behind them; flattening the image over paper inside the sampler made it mid-grey, which then replaced the band. Only a paint of alpha >= 0.999, Normal or Compatible, with no soft mask replaces the background.

spec units.luminance, Indexed (1.6, Codex v107 round 6; editor fixture, 279_indexed_lab.py): a checkerboard of an Indexed Lab palette - index 0 L* 0, index 1 lookup byte 255 - under a black box over the whole picture. A lookup byte spans its base component's range, L* 0..100 for Lab, so index 1 is L* 100, white: the picture under the box is intact (A6). Divided by 255 for every base, the white is L* 1, dark, the picture reads as blacked out and the file passes.

spec type3Glyphs, d0 colours (1.6, Codex v107 round 6; editor fixture, 280_type3_d0.py): a line in a Type 3 font whose glyph procedure begins with d0 and paints a white rectangle, shown with a black fill on white paper. A d0 glyph paints in its own colours, never the colour in force where it is shown: white on white, invisible and extractable (A4 same-as-background). Read in the caller's black, the line is visible and the file passes.
